title: Vegetable Biryani
subtitle: Fragrant layered rice with spiced vegetables
excerpt: Spiced vegetables and basmati rice cooked together with whole spices, saffron, and fried onions. A full and aromatic dish that works as a main course or a side.

recipe.sourceNotes: Biryani is a festive layered rice dish with origins in Mughal court cooking. The vegetable biryani is as celebrated in South India as the meat version is in the north. The hallmarks are the same: whole spices fried in oil, partially cooked rice layered with the main filling, and a tight seal on the pot to trap the steam for the final dum (slow cooking). Fried onions and saffron milk are the finishing touches.

recipeTools.notes: A heavy-based pan with a tight-fitting lid.

content.text: The rice is par-cooked first until just three-quarters done, then layered over the spiced vegetables and steamed to completion. This two-stage method keeps the grains separate. A tight seal is important for the final stage: place a sheet of foil under the lid to prevent steam escaping.

Fry the onion in 3 tablespoons of oil over high heat for 12 to 15 minutes until deep golden and beginning to crisp. Remove half for garnishing. Reduce to medium heat. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.

Add the garam masala, cumin, and turmeric. Stir for 1 minute. Add the potatoes, cauliflower, and carrot. Season with 1 teaspoon of salt. Stir to coat. Add 100 ml of water, cover, and cook for 10 minutes. Add the frozen peas.
Meanwhile, bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Add the bay leaves and soaked rice. Cook for 6 minutes until three-quarters done: the grains should have a slight bite. Drain well.

Spoon the rice over the vegetables in an even layer. Place a sheet of foil over the pan and press the lid on top. Cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes. Do not lift the lid. Scatter with the reserved fried onions and fresh coriander before serving.
